facts.text: Mondrian Hong Kong is in the Tsim Sha Tsui district with quick access to key attractions and landmarks.
facts.excerpt: Situated in the vibrant Tsim Sha Tsui district with quick access to key attractions and landmarks

facts.text: Mondrian Hong Kong is the first Mondrian hotel in Greater China.
facts.excerpt: Mondrian Hong Kong marks the launch of the first Mondrian hotel in Greater China.

facts.text: The rooms reimagine heritage design motifs through a contemporary lens, against the backdrop of Victoria Harbour and the Hong Kong skyline.
facts.excerpt: reimagining heritage design motifs through a contemporary lens, against the stunning backdrop of Victoria Harbour and the Hong Kong skyline

facts.text: Rooms connect to the city's spirit through nuanced designs, local art and Victoria Harbour views.
facts.excerpt: connect to the city’s spirit through nuanced designs, local art, and stunning Victoria Harbour views

facts.text: The Harbour Suite offers 180-degree views of the harbour or the Hong Kong cityscape through oversized windows.
facts.excerpt: Take in the breathtaking 180° views of the harbor or the vibrant Hong Kong cityscape through the oversized windows.

facts.text: The Harbour Suite has a lounge area, a connecting bedroom and two washrooms, one with a bathtub.
facts.excerpt: The suite features a stylish lounge area for relaxation and entertaining, a connecting bedroom, and two washrooms—one with a relaxing bathtub.

facts.text: Harbour Suite guests receive a welcome drink and priority check-in.
facts.excerpt: Experience personalised service with a welcome drink and priority check-in

facts.text: The Roofgarden is an open-air social space for guests to unwind above the city.
facts.excerpt: Mondrian Hong Kong’s Roofgarden is an open-air social space designed for guests to unwind above the city.

facts.text: The Roofgarden offers views of Victoria Harbour and the Hong Kong skyline, a spot for sunrise, sunset or the city lights after dark.
facts.excerpt: Offering sweeping views of Victoria Harbour and the iconic Hong Kong skyline, it is an ideal spot to take in sunrise, sunset or the city’s glittering lights after dark.

facts.text: The Cornershop is a street-level space opposite the hotel dedicated to artistic pop-up experiences.
facts.excerpt: The Cornershop is a dynamic, street-level space opposite Mondrian Hong Kong that celebrates the possibilities of artistic pop-up experiences.

facts.text: The Cornershop is open to the public daily, free of charge, with no reservation required.
facts.excerpt: The Cornershop is open to the public daily, free of charge, and reservations are not required.

facts.text: The Cornershop presents rotating exhibitions, creative collaborations and community-led programmes spotlighting Hong Kong's arts scene.
facts.excerpt: presents rotating exhibitions, creative collaborations and community-led programmes that spotlight Hong Kong’s vibrant arts and creative scene

facts.text: The hotel regularly hosts cultural programmes, live music, DJ nights, brand collaborations and art-led experiences throughout the year.
facts.excerpt: Mondrian Hong Kong regularly hosts cultural programmes, live music performances, DJ nights, brand collaborations and art-led experiences throughout the year.

facts.text: Carna by Dario Cecchini is a contemporary Italian steak restaurant led by butcher Dario Cecchini, focused on premium cuts and nose-to-tail dining.
facts.excerpt: Carna by Dario Cecchini is our contemporary Italian steak restaurant led by legendary butcher Dario Cecchini, celebrating premium cuts and sustainable nose-to-tail dining.

facts.text: Avoca, on the 38th floor, serves creative cocktails and all-day dining.
facts.excerpt: Guests can also head to Avoca on the 38th floor for creative cocktails and all-day dining

facts.text: The Avenue of Stars and the Victoria Harbour waterfront are both within a six-minute walk.
facts.excerpt: The Avenue of Stars and Victoria Harbour waterfront are both within a six-minute walk.

facts.text: Kowloon Park is a five-minute walk from the hotel.
facts.excerpt: Kowloon Park is just a five-minute walk from the hotel.

facts.text: The hotel is a one-minute walk from the nearest MTR exit.
facts.excerpt: The hotel is just a one-minute walk from the nearest MTR exit

facts.text: The hotel is a 4-minute walk from Tsim Sha Tsui underground train station.
facts.excerpt: 4 minute walk from Tsim Sha Tsui underground train station

facts.text: The hotel does not have a spa or wellness centre.
facts.excerpt: The hotel does not have a spa or wellness centre.

facts.text: The hotel does not have a swimming pool.
facts.excerpt: Mondrian Hong Kong does not have a swimming pool.

facts.text: The hotel does not charge a resort fee.
facts.excerpt: Mondrian Hong Kong does not charge a resort fee.

facts.text: The concierge team curates City Hunts, a monthly insider's guide to Hong Kong.
facts.excerpt: You may also explore our City Hunts, a monthly insider’s guide curated by our team

facts.text: A 'Sleep Tight' spiced herbal Chinese tea is offered to help promote quality sleep.
facts.excerpt: Wind down with a special ‘Sleep Tight’ spiced herbal chinese tea to help promote quality sleep during your stay at Mondrian Hong Kong

facts.text: Babysitting can be arranged on request.
facts.excerpt: Babysitting services can be arranged upon request.

facts.text: Mondrian Hong Kong was awarded Green Key certification in November 2025.
facts.excerpt: In November 2025, Mondrian Hong Kong was awarded the Green Key certification

facts.text: Mondrian Hong Kong opened in March 2024.
facts.excerpt: Opened in March 2024, Mondrian Hong Kong is the brand’s first outpost in Greater China.

facts.text: The hotel occupies a tall, slender tower with triangular windows that previously housed the Panorama Hotel.
facts.excerpt: inside a tall and skinny tower with triangular windows that previously housed the long-running Panorama Hotel

facts.text: Amsterdam-based designer Karin Krautgartner and her studio byKK transformed the interiors with bold, saturated hues.
facts.excerpt: Amsterdam-based designer Karin Krautgartner and her studio, byKK, completely transformed the previously run-of-the-mill decor with unapologetically bold and saturated hues

facts.text: The lobby has a two-story-high mosaic of underwater dancers and an orbital chandelier.
facts.excerpt: a glassy lobby opens with a two-story-high mosaic of underwater dancers, while an orbital chandelier casts ribbons of light across the room

facts.text: Underwater murals run through the corridors.
facts.excerpt: whimsical underwater murals course through the corridors

facts.text: Staff uniforms were designed by Hongkonger Frances Yim of Three Pound Void, inspired by the city's industrial craftsmanship.
facts.excerpt: Designed by Hongkonger Frances Yim, of Three Pound Void, the ensembles channel chic urban streetwear inspired by the city’s industrial craftsmanship.

facts.text: Rooms feature washi-paper lamps, custom graphic rugs and hits of crimson and mustard.
facts.excerpt: bold hits of crimson and mustard, custom graphic rugs, washi-paper lamps

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler says families are not the target audience.
facts.excerpt: families are not the target audience
